---
title: "Collapse: everyone at the first table"
subtitle: "Catalog M-06"
description: "Prior mass near alpha = 0 gives a non-trivial prior probability that all units share one cluster. Prior collapse, P(K_J = 1), is not posterior collapse, Pr(K_J = 1 | data)."
toc: false
---

In the [restaurant](../dpm/crp.qmd), customer n + 1 opens a new table with probability
alpha / (alpha + n). When alpha is close to 0 that almost never happens, and every
customer ends up at the first table:
P(K_J = 1 | alpha) = ∏ i / (i + alpha) over i = 1, …, J − 1, which is .906 for
J = 79 and alpha = 0.02. A Gamma(a, b) prior on alpha keeps some mass near 0, so it
assigns a prior probability to this *collapse*: all J units in one cluster.

## Reading the panels

- **A. Mass near 0.** Gamma(1, 1) puts Pr(alpha < .1) = .095 below alpha = .1. The TSMM
  prior for "about five clusters" at J = 100 with the widest confidence setting (VIF 5,
  paper Table 2) puts .182 there: a vaguer statement about the number of clusters buys more
  mass near alpha = 0.
- **B. Prior collapse.** Under Gamma(1, 1), P(K_J = 1) is .192 at J = 50, .175 at J = 79,
  .168 at J = 100 and .132 at J = 500. Under the VIF 5 prior it is .262, .247, .240 and
  .204.
- **C. The restaurant at small alpha.** Press **Play** (or Enter): at alpha = 0.02 all 79
  customers usually share one table. Switch the restaurant alpha to 0.1 or 1 and play again.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Prior versus posterior collapse.** P(K_J = 1) is a prior statement, made before any data.
Pr(K_J = 1 | data) is a posterior statement about a fitted model. For STAR (79 schools)
under Gamma(1, 1) the prior value is .175 and the released posterior value is .560; the
widget reads the posterior value from the replication package and does not recompute it.
K_J is the number of fitted components (occupied clusters) among the J units.
:::

Standalone version: [embed/collapse.html](../../embed/collapse.html), for example
`?preset=vif5` or `?a=0.5&b=0.5`.
